name: Geierwally Freilichtbühne Elbigenalp
kurzbeschreibung: The Geierwally-Freilichtbühne in Elbigenalp: spectacular open-air theater stage in the wild Bernhardstalschlucht in honor of Anna Stainer-Knittel.
beschreibung:
Overview

The dramatic Geierwally-Freilichtbühne is nestled deep between the rugged rock faces of the romantic Bernhardstalschlucht gorge in the municipality of Elbigenalp in Tyrol's Lechtal (Reutte district) at an altitude of around 1,040 meters. Founded in 1993, this acclaimed natural open-air stage is one of the most extraordinary and atmospheric cultural venues in the entire Alpine region. Erected in honor of the famous Lechtal painter and pioneer Anna Stainer-Knittel (1841–1915) – who achieved worldwide fame as the legendary "Geierwally" through Wilhelmine von Hillern's novel –, the stage captivates thousands of theater and culture enthusiasts from across Central Europe every year.

Gorge Stage & Anna Stainer-Knittel

The historical inspiration for the stage is rooted in a true event: as a 17-year-old girl in 1858, Anna Stainer-Knittel was lowered on a rope down a vertical rock face in the Lechtaler Alpen to retrieve an eagle's nest – a daring feat that no man dared attempt at the time. Literature transformed this event into the archetype of the courageous, indomitable Alpine heroine. The open-air stage utilizes the sheer limestone crags of the Bernhardstalschlucht and the rushing mountain waters of the Bernhardstalbach stream as a monumental, natural backdrop. Thanks to a state-of-the-art weatherproof umbrella canopy installed in 2018, the approximately 600 spectator seats are sheltered from rain without compromising the unique open-air atmosphere and breathtaking gorge acoustics. Every summer from early July to late August, the ensemble stages high-caliber new productions of Tyrolean folk plays, dramas, musicals, and classical works. Directly along the approach path to the stage, a small thematic trail illustrates the life, botanical watercolors, and emancipatory legacy of Anna Stainer-Knittel.

Visit & Getting There

The theater season at the Geierwally-Freilichtbühne runs annually from early July to late August with performances on weekends (Friday to Sunday, typically starting at 20:30; afternoon performances on Sundays at 15:00). Ticket prices for theater performances (2025/2026 season): approx. €28.00 to €38.00 depending on category. Outside performance times, the gorge area and themed trail are open during daylight hours and accessible free of charge. Getting there by car: via the B198 (Lechtalstraße) from Reutte or Warth to Elbigenalp; large free parking lots are available in the village center near the municipal center (from there it is an easy 10-minute walk into the Bernhardstalschlucht). By public transport: take the ÖBB train to Reutte in Tirol station, then transfer to Postbus line 110 through the Lechtal directly to the Elbigenalp Gemeindeamt stop.

Tips

The illuminated path through the gorge to the grandstand is surfaced with wide gravel and is accessible for wheelchair users with slight companion assistance (dedicated wheelchair spaces are available in the covered theater area). As performances take place in a cool mountain gorge, bringing a warm jacket or blanket is highly recommended even on warm midsummer evenings. Be sure to book theater tickets well in advance, as many performances sell out weeks beforehand.
